standard_prerequisites.name: Automatic-homotopy lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a = a is a set, every x is merely equal to a and q commutes with all self-paths, then there is f : prd x:X (x = x) with f(a) = q.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied to the type X and the point a at source line 129.

standard_prerequisites.name: No higher axiom of choice
standard_prerequisites.statement: The type Sigma A:type, brck(bool = A) is used earlier in the book to refute a higher form of the axiom of choice.
standard_prerequisites.use: The same type is reused here at source line 125.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalences of the booleans
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every equivalence bool ~ bool is equal to the identity or to the swapping equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at source line 132 for the four-way case analysis.

core_obligations: Reduce to exhibiting a type X with prd x:X (x = x) not a mere proposition, and take X := Sigma A:type, brck(bool = A) (source lines 124-125).
It suffices to produce f : prd x:X (x = x) unequal to the constant reflexivity map (source line 126).
Set a := (bool, |refl bool|) and let q : a = a be the path corresponding to the swapping equivalence of bool (source line 128).

Check the three hypotheses of the retained auto-homotopy lemma: a = a is equivalent to the set of equivalences bool ~ bool, every x : X is merely equal to a, and centrality follows from the classification of the equivalences of bool by a four-way case analysis (source lines 130-132).

Conclude f : prd x:X (x = x) with f(a) = q, and since the swapping equivalence is not the identity, q is not refl a, so f is not the constant map and the type of self-paths is not a mere proposition (source lines 134-136).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to a type with a non-propositional type of self-paths and choose the candidate type.
Choose the point and the path q, and verify the three hypotheses of the retained lemma.
Compare f with the constant map and conclude.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled theorem `thm:qinv-notprop` at source lines 120-122: there are types A, B and a function f with qinv(f) not a mere proposition. The author's proof (source lines 123-137) is a construction in three layers: it first reduces the goal to a type X whose self-path type is not a proposition and picks X := Sigma A:type, brck(bool = A) (lines 124-125), then chooses the point a and the path q coming from the swapping equivalence of the booleans (line 128), and then verifies the three hypotheses of the retained auto-homotopy lemma one by one (lines 130-132): the self-path type of a is equivalent to the set of equivalences of bool, the point is merely connected to every other point of X, and centrality is a four-way case analysis based on the classification of the equivalences of bool. The final step compares the resulting f with the constant reflexivity map (lines 134-136). The statement says only that a counterexample exists.
